subject: Rejecting initial values in plain multi_normal_cholesky

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Rejecting initial values in plain multi_normal_cholesky
parts:
The model is just a plain multivariate normal but I'm getting the "Stan
can't start sampling from this initial value" error when the dimensions
are greater than 45. The program code is adapted from section 6.14, p.
78. Am I making a typo somewhere?

Program code:


data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1> K;
vector[K] y[N];
}
parameters {
cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega; // prior corr
vector<lower=0>[K] L_sigma; // prior scale
}
model {
matrix[K,K] L_Sigma;

L_Sigma <- diag_pre_multiply(L_sigma, L_Omega);

L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(4);
L_sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);

y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(rep_vector(0, K), L_Sigma);
}


Thanks,

Allen

parts:
I think this might pin down the problem. I changed the code to be a bit
more explicit:

data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1> K;
vector[K] y[N];
}
parameters {
cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega; // prior corr
vector<lower=0>[K] L_sigma; // prior scale
}

transformed parameters {
cholesky_factor_cov[K] L_Sigma;
L_Sigma <- diag_pre_multiply(L_sigma, L_Omega);
}
model {
L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);

L_sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);

y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(rep_vector(0, K), L_Sigma);
}

And I get more helpful errors like:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
validate transformed params: L_Sigma is 0, but must be > 0!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Rejecting initial value:
Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value.


Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts.
Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model.
